### The Multi-Year Compute Crunch

From founders setting up AI servers next to their wine cellars, to the biggest companies rationing compute, everyone is scrambling. [...] Everyone is chasing compute, per the WSJ in ‘The Desperate Hunt for AI Computing Power Is Upending Silicon Valley’. Even at the top of the heap, budgeting compute across teams is a big challenge. Google lost one of its star AI researchers, Noam Shazeer, whom it paid $2.7 billion in 2024 to bring back, when he left for OpenAI after his team’s compute was cut. Renting Nvidia’s older H100 chips on a one-year contract costs about 60% more than a year ago, per SemiAnalysis. Cloud providers now want [...] Cheaper isn’t always cheaper. Researchers at Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, Berkeley and Microsoft Research tested more than 6,800 tasks and found that in 32% of cases, the lower-priced AI model ended up costing more. In one test, Google’s Gemini 3 Flash ran 952 steps, spent about $14, and failed; Gemini 3.1 Pro finished in 85 steps, for about $1. And the same model can use a different number of tokens each time it runs the same task. Google points customers to spending caps and flexible pricing.

highlights: # Anthropic revenue surges 45% to nearly $17B in third quarter as AI giant gears up for IPO. Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an investor who attended a pre-IPO meeting with Anthropic leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday. Revenue in the first quarter was $4.7 billion, and $11.6 billion in the second quarter, according to the person who attended the investor day meant to familiarize prospective Anthropic investors before its highly anticipated IPO. The IPO is expected to precede a public listing by rival OpenAI, making Anthropic an early test of investor appetite for heavily unprofitable AI developers pursuing massive scale. Founded by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. Anthropic has also sought to distinguish itself through its focus on AI safety, warning of the dangers posed by increasingly capable systems even as it competes in the race to develop and commercialize more powerful models.

Brin pointed to the releases of Google's Flash models before Gemini 4 as evidence that this was happening, and said the company was "starting to get onto that RSI treadmill.". Anthropic and OpenAI have also said that AI may be on the verge of RSI. In a safety report for its new Argon model, Google said that some components of the AI research and development cycle were getting automated. highlights: MP Take: the frontier companies are recognizing it. OpenAI’s newer default models cut sycophancy by more than two-thirds, and outside researchers are seeing the improvement.
### The Multi-Year Compute Crunch

From founders setting up AI servers next to their wine cellars, to the biggest companies rationing compute, everyone is scrambling. [...] Everyone is chasing compute, per the WSJ in ‘The Desperate Hunt for AI Computing Power Is Upending Silicon Valley’. Even at the top of the heap, budgeting compute across teams is a big challenge. Google lost one of its star AI researchers, Noam Shazeer, whom it paid $2.7 billion in 2024 to bring back, when he left for OpenAI after his team’s compute was cut. Renting Nvidia’s older H100 chips on a one-year contract costs about 60% more than a year ago, per SemiAnalysis. Cloud providers now want [...] Cheaper isn’t always cheaper. Researchers at Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, Berkeley and Microsoft Research tested more than 6,800 tasks and found that in 32% of cases, the lower-priced AI model ended up costing more. In one test, Google’s Gemini 3 Flash ran 952 steps, spent about $14, and failed; Gemini 3.1 Pro finished in 85 steps, for about $1. And the same model can use a different number of tokens each time it runs the same task. Google points customers to spending caps and flexible pricing.

week.title: Anthropic revenue surges 45% to nearly $17B in third quarter as AI giant gears up for IPO - New York Post
week.summary: # Anthropic revenue surges 45% to nearly $17B in third quarter as AI giant gears up for IPO. Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an inve...
highlights: # Anthropic revenue surges 45% to nearly $17B in third quarter as AI giant gears up for IPO. Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an investor who attended a pre-IPO meeting with Anthropic leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday. Revenue in the first quarter was $4.7 billion, and $11.6 billion in the second quarter, according to the person who attended the investor day meant to familiarize prospective Anthropic investors before its highly anticipated IPO. The IPO is expected to precede a public listing by rival OpenAI, making Anthropic an early test of investor appetite for heavily unprofitable AI developers pursuing massive scale. Founded by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. Anthropic has also sought to distinguish itself through its focus on AI safety, warning of the dangers posed by increasingly capable systems even as it competes in the race to develop and commercialize more powerful models.

week.title: Anthropic's quarterly revenue leaps to $16.8 billion as IPO looms - Business Insider
week.summary: Anthropic told investors it brought in $16.8 billion in revenue during the third quarter, Business Insider has learned. The company behind Claude said Wednesday that it achieved profitability on an ad...
highlights: Anthropic told investors it brought in $16.8 billion in revenue during the third quarter, Business Insider has learned. The company behind Claude said Wednesday that it achieved profitability on an adjusted basis last quarter. Investors view Anthropic's revenue as a proxy for the company's competition with OpenAI, and for the strength of an early AI market that has boosted stocks by trillions of dollars in value. It's unclear if the new revenue tally counts gross or net revenue, or how Anthropic arrived at its definition of profitability. The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Anthropic brought in $4.8 billion in revenue in the first quarter, then more than doubled it to around $11.6 billion in the second quarter. Since Anthropic is still private, these glimpses at revenue are a crucial stand-in for investors considering the coming IPO and AI's impact on other stocks. A torrent of state-of-the-art AI models and strong adoption of the AI coding tool Claude Code have propelled Anthropic's fortunes, making it one of the fastest-growing companies in history.

month.summary:
MP Take: the frontier companies are recognizing it. OpenAI’s newer default models cut sycophancy by more than two-thirds, and outside researchers are seeing the improvement.

### The Multi-Year Comput...
highlights: MP Take: the frontier companies are recognizing it. OpenAI’s newer default models cut sycophancy by more than two-thirds, and outside researchers are seeing the improvement.
### The Multi-Year Compute Crunch

From founders setting up AI servers next to their wine cellars, to the biggest companies rationing compute, everyone is scrambling. [...] Everyone is chasing compute, per the WSJ in ‘The Desperate Hunt for AI Computing Power Is Upending Silicon Valley’. Even at the top of the heap, budgeting compute across teams is a big challenge. Google lost one of its star AI researchers, Noam Shazeer, whom it paid $2.7 billion in 2024 to bring back, when he left for OpenAI after his team’s compute was cut. Renting Nvidia’s older H100 chips on a one-year contract costs about 60% more than a year ago, per SemiAnalysis. Cloud providers now want [...] Cheaper isn’t always cheaper. Researchers at Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, Berkeley and Microsoft Research tested more than 6,800 tasks and found that in 32% of cases, the lower-priced AI model ended up costing more. In one test, Google’s Gemini 3 Flash ran 952 steps, spent about $14, and failed; Gemini 3.1 Pro finished in 85 steps, for about $1. And the same model can use a different number of tokens each time it runs the same task. Google points customers to spending caps and flexible pricing.
